title: Ingestion file formats
text: Nimbus RAG ingestion accepts PDF, Markdown, and plain-text files. Files larger than 20 MB are rejected before parsing. HTML ingestion is not enabled in the reference pipeline.

title: Chunking policy
text: The default chunk size is 600 tokens with an overlap of 80 tokens. Chunk boundaries prefer paragraph endings when one occurs near the target size. Chunking is deterministic for the same normalized input.

title: Embedding model
text: The reference embedding configuration uses the text-embedding-3-small model. Embeddings are generated asynchronously by the worker. The embedding model name is stored with every indexed chunk.

title: Vector storage
text: Chunk embeddings are stored in PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension. The chunks table keeps document id, chunk text, embedding vector, model name, and created timestamp. Similarity search uses cosine distance.

title: Async jobs
text: Embedding jobs run in a Celery worker. Redis is the Celery broker and carries task messages between the API process and workers. Failed embedding tasks retry up to three times with exponential backoff.

title: Retrieval defaults
text: The query service retrieves the top 5 chunks by default. Retrieval uses cosine similarity over pgvector and can optionally filter by document id. The top-k value can be overridden per request.

title: Query API
text: POST /query accepts a question and optional top_k value. The endpoint returns the generated answer, retrieved chunk identifiers, source document identifiers, and latency metadata. A request id is included for tracing.

title: Ingestion API
text: POST /documents creates an ingestion job and returns HTTP 202 with a job id. GET /jobs/{job_id} reports queued, running, succeeded, or failed status. The API does not block while embeddings are created.

title: Prompt versioning
text: Query prompts live in versioned files under the prompts directory, such as v1_query.txt and v2_query.txt. Each evaluation run records the prompt version. Prompt text is reviewed in Git like application code.

title: MLflow tracking
text: MLflow logs retrieval experiments including recall@k, mean reciprocal rank, chunk size, embedding model, and prompt version. The best configuration can be registered in the MLflow model registry as an evaluation artifact.

title: Local services
text: The Docker Compose stack starts PostgreSQL with pgvector, Redis, the FastAPI service, a Celery worker, and MLflow. The API depends on the database and Redis health checks before startup.

title: Health endpoints
text: GET /health is a liveness check and returns ok when the API process is running. GET /ready checks PostgreSQL and Redis connectivity. Readiness returns a non-200 status when either dependency is unavailable.

title: Document identifiers
text: Every ingested document receives a stable UUID document id. Re-ingesting the same source creates a new ingestion version while preserving the source URI in metadata. Chunk ids are unique per ingestion version.

title: Deletion behavior
text: DELETE /documents/{document_id} removes the document and all of its chunks from the active index. Deletion is idempotent: deleting an already absent document returns success with deleted=false.

title: Metadata filters
text: The retriever supports equality filters for document id, source type, and collection. Metadata filters are applied before vector ranking. Arbitrary SQL expressions are not accepted from query clients.

title: Rate limits
text: The reference API allows 60 query requests per minute per API key. Ingestion is limited to 10 new documents per minute per API key. Clients that exceed a limit receive HTTP 429.

title: Observability
text: Structured logs include request id, route, status code, and latency. Query traces also record retrieval duration and generation duration. Secrets and full embedding vectors are excluded from logs.

title: Evaluation dataset
text: The golden evaluation set is stored as JSONL. Each row contains an id, question, known-correct reference answer, relevant document ids, and answer keywords used by the deterministic fixture.

title: Retrieval metrics
text: Retrieval quality is measured with precision@k, recall@k, and mean reciprocal rank. Precision@k measures how many retrieved items are relevant, recall@k measures how many relevant items were recovered, and reciprocal rank rewards an early first relevant result.

title: CI regression gate
text: Continuous integration runs the deterministic evaluation harness on every push and pull request. The job exits with status 1 when any configured metric falls below its minimum threshold. The JSON report is uploaded as a CI artifact.
